sources.title: RFC 8259: The JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) Data Interchange Format

beats.goal: The learner knows JSON values have types.
beats.content: Every JSON value has a type: object, array, string, number, boolean or null.

beats.goal: The learner knows quotes make a string.
beats.content: A value in double quotes is a string, even when it looks like a number: "42" is a string, 42 is a number.
beats.question: Which of these is a string in JSON, 42 or "42"?

checkpoint.question: What is the difference between {"port": 8080} and {"port": "8080"}?
checkpoint.rubric: A good answer says the first value is a number and the second a string.

branches.when: The answer names number versus string.
The answer names number versus string and the learner already knows booleans.
branches.message: Right. You can skip ahead to fixing a config file.

branches.when: The answer misses the number/string difference.
branches.message: Let's go over the value types once more.
